notes:
=== CONCEPT ===
mount -t nfs mounts a remote NFS export as a local directory, providing direct filesystem access. After mounting, ls -n reveals numeric UID/GID of files — the foundation for the UID matching attack.

=== UID MATCHING ATTACK ===
ls -n shows file owned by UID 1000 → create local user with UID 1000 on attacker machine → now have read/write to those files on the mount. NFS trusts whatever UID/GID the client presents.

=== no_root_squash EXPLOITATION ===
If no_root_squash is set: attacker root uploads SUID shell binary to NFS share → target SSH user executes binary → binary runs with elevated UID → privilege escalation.

=== CHAINING ===
showmount -e → identify exports → mount share → ls -n for UIDs → match UIDs locally → access/modify files → if writable + no_root_squash: place SUID binary for privesc.
